title: Parity of a Mixed-Degree Polynomial f(x) = x^2 + x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the function f(x) = x^2 + x is even, odd, or neither, and justify your answer.

steps.title: Evaluate f(-x)
steps.explanation: Substitute -x into f(x) = x^2 + x to obtain f(-x) = x^2 - x.
steps.why: The quadratic term x^2 is unchanged by negation while the linear term x changes sign.

steps.title: Compare f(-x) with f(x) and -f(x)
steps.mathExpression: f(-x) = x^2 - x \ne x^2 + x = f(x), \quad f(-x) = x^2 - x \ne -x^2 - x = -f(x)
steps.explanation: For example, at x = 1, f(1) = 2 while f(-1) = (-1)^2 + (-1) = 0, which equals neither 2 nor -2.
steps.why: A single counterexample x = 1 suffices to show that neither f(-x) = f(x) nor f(-x) = -f(x) holds identically.

steps.title: Conclude Function Parity
steps.explanation: Because f(-x) equals neither f(x) nor -f(x), the function f(x) = x^2 + x is neither even nor odd.
steps.why: The sum of a non-zero even function (x^2) and a non-zero odd function (x) is neither even nor odd.
